claims.text: Replicated state machines are typically implemented using a replicated log. Each server stores a log containing a series of commands, which its state machine executes in order.

Each log contains the same commands in the same order, so each state machine processes the same sequence of commands. Because the state machines are deterministic, each computes the same state and the same sequence of outputs.
Keeping the replicated log consistent is the job of the consensus algorithm.

Raft first elects a distinguished leader and gives it complete responsibility for managing the replicated log. The leader accepts log entries from clients, replicates them on other servers, and tells servers when it is safe to apply them.

A log entry is committed once the leader that created it has replicated it on a majority of the servers. Raft guarantees that committed entries are durable and will eventually be executed by all of the available state machines.

Election Safety: at most one leader can be elected in a given term. Leader Completeness: if a log entry is committed in a given term, it will be present in the logs of the leaders for all higher-numbered terms.

Consensus algorithms for practical systems are fully functional as long as any majority of the servers are operational and can communicate with each other and with clients. A typical cluster of five servers can tolerate the failure of any two.

Coinbase Derivatives Exchange treats its trading system as a deterministic state machine: a state plus an input always gives the same next state and output, so the system can be snapshotted, restored and replayed to reach its live state.
It gets fault tolerance from Raft using Aeron Cluster, which requires the application to be deterministic and single threaded.

Its engineers list data structure iteration order, randomness and behaviour changes between versions as the things that make determinism tricky. Old input must produce old behaviour, which they handle with feature flagging.

recall.prompt: Why do replicas that apply the same log end up in the same state?

answer.text: Each log holds the same commands in the same order and the state machines are deterministic, so each computes the same state and the same outputs.

recall.prompt: When is a Raft log entry committed?

answer.text: Once the leader that created it has replicated it on a majority of the servers.

recall.prompt: How many failures can a five-server cluster tolerate, and why?

answer.text: Any two, because the system is fully functional as long as any majority of the servers are operational.

recall.prompt: What does Coinbase say breaks determinism in a trading system?

answer.text: Data structure iteration order, randomness, and behaviour changes between versions.
